caption: The drawing depicts a mechanical device composed primarily of wood and metal components, illustrated in natural brown and grayish hues. The main body of the device consists of a cylindrical transparent chamber, likely made of glass, seated on a round wooden base. Four vertical, turned wooden pillars support a horizontal wooden frame at the top. At the top front, there is a cranked handle attached to a gearbox featuring visible cogs and gears, which interact with internal mechanisms visible inside the glass chamber. Two smaller, technical drawings are included below the main illustration: one to the left, a front view with dimensions marked as "7 inches" and "11 inches," and one to the right, a frontal elevation view with additional dimensions such as "9½ inches," "20¼ inches," and "11½ inches." Both technical drawings are rendered in thin black lines, while the main perspective illustration uses shading for depth and realism, with the artist’s signature "F. Ward" visible below the right technical sketch. The background is a plain, pale beige color throughout.
title: Butter Churn
